audience: OpenCode is for people who want a coding agent in the terminal, a desktop app, or a local web UI, and who are willing to bring a model. The verdict is specific: the agent is free under the MIT license, and the bill is either your own provider or OpenCode Go at $10 a month. Go Plus is $40 a month when the $10 caps are too small.

It is a poor fit if you wanted one shared allowance and a team on the same Go workspace. The Go docs say a workspace with a Go subscription cannot invite members, and each model has its own monthly dollar limit.
features: The OpenCode row is Free under the MIT license on github.com/anomalyco/opencode. The v2 docs describe a terminal interface, a desktop app, and a local web UI opened with the opencode pair command. You do not buy a seat to install it.

Go is $10 a month. Go Plus is $40 a month. Both figures are on opencode.ai/go, checked 15 October 2026. The docs say Go is optional and works like any other provider: you subscribe, copy a key, and connect it. You can also point OpenCode at a provider you already pay.

Zen is the pay-as-you-go catalog. opencode.ai/zen says to add a $20 balance, plus a $1.23 card fee, and that another $20 is added when the balance reaches $5. The v2 billing page lists Console packs of $10, $50, and $100, a processing fee of 4.6% plus $0.31, and no seat fee. That $1.23 on a $20 top-up is the same fee formula, not a second price we invented.
limitations: Go limits are monthly dollar amounts per model. The docs say 20% of a model's monthly limit can be used in any 5 hours, and 50% in a week. A $10 plan can still stop you on one model while another model has room left. We do not reprint the per-model table, because it is a long list and it is not one pool.

A Go workspace is for a single member. Teams that want seats should look at a product that sells them. OpenCode 1 and OpenCode 2 both use the opencode command and cannot be installed side by side under that default command, which the docs say outright.

The rating is Depends. Depends means the client is free and the model is not. Claude Pro, which includes Claude Code, is $20 a month. GitHub Copilot Pro is $10 a month. If your key spend is already past those seats, the MIT license is not the cheaper product.
pricingNotes: Checked 15 October 2026. OpenCode is Free under MIT. Go is $10 a month and Go Plus is $40 a month on opencode.ai/go. Zen starts with a $20 balance plus a $1.23 card fee on opencode.ai/zen. Your own provider is pay that provider. No annual Go price is printed on the Go page, so none is shown.

The Go docs define the caps as monthly dollar amounts per model, with a 5-hour slice of 20% and a weekly slice of 50%. Console credit packs of $10, $50, and $100, and the 4.6% plus $0.31 processing fee, are on the v2 billing docs. Requests fail when a prepaid balance hits zero.

alternatives.text: is the terminal agent that comes with a Claude plan. Pro is $20 a month, or $17 a month billed annually with $200 up front, and it includes Claude Code. Max starts from $100 a month. Choose it when you want an included allowance instead of a per-model Go cap.

is the other free terminal tool. It is Apache-2.0, and you pay your API provider with no included allowance. OpenCode adds a $10 Go plan and a desktop app. Aider stays a terminal pair programmer with no seat.
is Apache-2.0 as well. The tool is free and you pay the provider, including a local model if you connect one. It is the closer cousin if you want an IDE extension and a CLI without a Go subscription.

is the editor. Docs list Pro at $20, Pro Plus at $60, and Ultra at $200, and the public pricing page showed a different lineup. Depends, until those two pages agree. Use it when you want the IDE, and read that mismatch before you pay.

faqs.a: The agent is free under the MIT license. Go, the optional model plan, is $10 a month. Go Plus is $40 a month. Zen is a prepaid balance, starting at $20 plus a $1.23 card fee. A provider you connect yourself bills you directly.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Go and Go Plus?
faqs.a: The price is $10 a month versus $40 a month. The docs say both plans reach the same models, and Go Plus has higher monthly dollar limits on those models. The limits are still per model.

faqs.q: Can a team share one Go plan?
faqs.a: No. The Go docs say Go and Go Plus are for a workspace with a single member, and a workspace with a Go subscription cannot invite members.

faqs.q: Does OpenCode have an affiliate link?
faqs.a: No. We did not find a public publisher affiliate signup on opencode.ai. The Visit button goes to opencode.ai.
